translations.literal: But when an imperial rescript comes down, the ministers in the hall dare not openly defy it, the censor-remonstrators dare not probe deeply, and the drafting secretariat dare not stand firm—because such matters concern the favored and powerful, and they deeply fear that any opening might provoke fresh offense and graver punishment.
translations.idiomatic: But when an imperial rescript comes down, the ministers in the hall dare not openly defy it, the censor-remonstrators dare not probe deeply, and the drafting secretariat dare not stand firm—because such matters touch the favored and powerful, and they deeply fear that any opening might provoke fresh offense and graver punishment.

sentences.zh: 故凡勸導人主事從中出者，蓋欲假人主之聲勢，以漸竊威權耳。

translations.literal: Thus everyone who counsels the ruler while acting from behind the throne seeks to borrow the sovereign's authority and renown in order gradually to seize power for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thus everyone who counsels the ruler while acting from behind the throne seeks to borrow the sovereign's authority and prestige in order gradually to seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 比者聞之道路，左右褻禦，於黜陟廢置之際，間得聞者，車馬輻湊，其門如市，恃權怙寵，搖撼外庭。

translations.literal: Lately one hears on the road that attendants close to the sovereign, when appointments and dismissals are decided and word occasionally leaks out, find their gates thronged with carriages and horses like a marketplace—relying on power and favor, they shake the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Lately one hears on the road that attendants close to the sovereign, when appointments and dismissals are decided and word occasionally leaks out, find their gates thronged with carriages and horses like a marketplace—relying on power and favor, they shake the outer court.

sentences.zh: 臣恐事勢浸淫，政歸幸門，不在公室。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the situation will worsen by degrees until government rests with the favorites' doors, not with the public administration.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the situation will worsen by degrees until government rests with the favorites' doors, not with the public administration.

sentences.zh: 凡所薦進皆其所私，凡所傾陷皆其所惡，豈但側目憚畏，莫敢指言，而阿比順從，內外表裏之患，必將形見。

translations.literal: Everyone they advance is their own protégé; everyone they ruin is their enemy. Not only will men watch sideways in fear and dare not speak—but fawning and collusion, the harm within and without, will surely become visible.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone they advance is their own protégé; everyone they ruin is their enemy. Not only will men watch sideways in fear and dare not speak—but fawning and collusion, the harm within and without, will surely become visible.

sentences.zh: 臣因李祥獲罪而深及此者，是豈矯激自取罪戾哉？

translations.literal: I speak at such length because Li Xiang was punished—is this merely reckless exaggeration to bring guilt upon myself?
translations.idiomatic: I speak at such length because Li Xiang was punished—is this merely reckless exaggeration to bring guilt upon myself?

sentences.zh: 實以士氣頹靡之中，稍忤權臣，則去不旋踵。

translations.literal: In truth, with the spirit of the scholar-official class already sagging, a slight offense against a powerful minister means dismissal almost at once.
translations.idiomatic: In truth, with the spirit of the scholar-official class already sagging, a slight offense against a powerful minister means dismissal almost at once.

sentences.zh: 私憂過計，深慮陛下之勢孤，而相與維持宗社者浸寡也。”

translations.literal: Out of private anxiety I may overstate the case, yet I deeply fear that Your Majesty stands increasingly alone, and those who jointly uphold the altars of state grow ever fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Out of private anxiety I may overstate the case, yet I deeply fear that Your Majesty stands increasingly alone, and those who jointly uphold the altars of state grow ever fewer.

sentences.zh: 疏既上，束簷待罪。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, he tied himself at the eaves and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was submitted, he bound himself at the eaves and awaited punishment.

sentences.zh: 有旨：呂祖儉朋比罔上，安置韶州。

translations.literal: An edict came: Lü Zujian had formed factions and deceived his sovereign; he was to be settled at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down: Lü Zujian had formed factions and deceived his sovereign; he was to be settled at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人鄧馹繳奏，祖儉罪不至貶。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Deng Zhi submitted a rebuttal memorial: Zujian's offense did not warrant demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Deng Zhi submitted a rebuttal memorial, arguing that Zujian's offense did not warrant demotion.

sentences.zh: 御筆：“祖儉意在無君，罪當誅。

translations.literal: Imperial rescript: "Zujian's intent is disloyalty to his ruler; the crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rescript: "Zujian's intent is disloyalty to his ruler; the crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 竄逐已為寬恩。”

translations.literal: Banishment is already a lenient show of mercy."
translations.idiomatic: Banishment is already a lenient show of mercy."

sentences.zh: 會樓鑰進讀呂公著元祐初所上十事，因進曰：“如公著社稷臣，猶將十世宥之，前日太府寺丞呂祖儉以言事得罪者，其孫也。

translations.literal: Then Lou Yue, while reading aloud to the throne Lü Gongzhu's ten memorial items from the early Yuanyou era, added: "If even a pillar of state like Gongzhu should receive pardon for ten generations, Vice Director Lü Zujian, who was punished for speaking out the other day, is his grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lou Yue, while reading aloud to the throne Lü Gongzhu's ten memorial items from the early Yuanyou era, added, "If even a pillar of state like Gongzhu should receive pardon for ten generations, Vice Director Lü Zujian, who was punished for speaking out the other day, is his grandson.

sentences.zh: 今投之嶺外，萬一即死，聖朝有殺言者之名，臣竊為陛下惜之。”

translations.literal: Now, if he is sent beyond the mountain passes and should die, the dynasty will bear the name of slaying those who speak—I am deeply concerned for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Now, if he is sent beyond the mountain passes and should die, the dynasty will bear the name of slaying those who speak—I am deeply concerned for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上問：“祖儉所言何事？”

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "What did Zujian speak about?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What did Zujian speak about?"

sentences.zh: 然後知前日之行不出上意。

translations.literal: Only then did he realize that the action the other day had not come from the emperor's own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he realize that the action the other day had not come from the emperor's own intent.

sentences.zh: 侂胄謂人曰：“復有救祖儉者，當處以新州矣。”

translations.literal: Tuozhou said to others: "If anyone again tries to save Zujian, he shall be sent to Xin Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou said to others, "If anyone again tries to save Zujian, he shall be sent to Xin Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢出口。

translations.literal: No one dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 有謂侂胄曰：“自趙丞相去，天下已切齒，今又投祖儉瘴鄉，不幸或死，則怨益重，曷若少徙內地。”

translations.literal: Someone told Tuozhou: "Since Chief Minister Zhao was removed, the realm has already gnashed its teeth; now, if Zujian is sent to the malarial south and should unhappily die, resentment will only deepen—would it not be better to transfer him somewhat inward?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Tuozhou, "Since Chief Minister Zhao was removed, the realm has already gnashed its teeth; now, if Zujian is sent to the malarial south and should unhappily die, resentment will only deepen—would it not be better to transfer him somewhat inward?"

sentences.zh: 侂胄亦悟。

translations.literal: Tuozhou came to see the point.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou came to see the point.

sentences.zh: 祖儉至廬陵，將趨嶺，得旨改送吉州。

translations.literal: Zujian reached Luling and was about to cross the passes when an order came to send him instead to Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zujian reached Luling and was about to cross the mountain passes when an order came to send him instead to Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，量移高安。

translations.literal: A general amnesty came; he was transferred as permitted to Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty came, and he was transferred as permitted to Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，詔令歸葬。

translations.literal: Two years later he died; an edict ordered his remains returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died; an edict ordered his remains returned for burial.

sentences.zh: 祖儉之謫也，朱熹與書曰：“熹以官則高於子約，以上之顧遇恩禮則深於子約，然坐視群小之為，不能一言以報效，乃令子約獨舒憤懣，觸群小而蹈禍機，其愧歎深矣。”

translations.literal: When Zujian was in exile, Zhu Xi wrote to him: "In rank I am higher than you, Ziyue, and in the favor and courtesy the sovereign has shown me I am treated more deeply than you—yet I sit by while petty men do as they please, unable to speak a single word in service, and let you alone pour out your indignation, provoke those petty men, and walk into the jaws of disaster. My shame and sighing run deep."
translations.idiomatic: When Zujian was in exile, Zhu Xi wrote to him, "In rank I am higher than you, Ziyue, and in the favor and courtesy the sovereign has shown me I am treated more deeply than you—yet I sit by while petty men do as they please, unable to speak a single word in service, and let you alone pour out your indignation, provoke those petty men, and walk into the jaws of disaster. My shame and sighing run deep."

sentences.zh: 祖儉報書曰：“在朝行聞時事，如在水火中，不可一朝居。

translations.literal: Zujian replied: "While at court one hears of current affairs as if living amid water and fire—it cannot be endured for a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Zujian replied, "While at court one hears of current affairs as if living amid water and fire—it cannot be endured for a single morning.

sentences.zh: 使處鄉閭，理亂不知，又何以多言為哉？”

translations.literal: If one dwells in the countryside and does not know whether order or chaos prevails, what point is there in speaking much?"
translations.idiomatic: If one dwells in the countryside and does not know whether order or chaos prevails, what point is there in speaking much?"

sentences.zh: 在謫所，讀書窮理，賣藥以自給。

translations.literal: At his place of exile he studied books to exhaust principle and sold medicine to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile he studied books to exhaust principle and sold medicine to support himself.

sentences.zh: 每出，必草履徒步，為逾嶺之備。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out, he always wore straw sandals and walked on foot, preparing himself to cross the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out, he always wore straw sandals and walked on foot, preparing himself to cross the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 嚐言：“因世變有所摧折，失其素履者，固不足言矣；

translations.literal: He once said: "Those broken by the changes of the times and who lose their lifelong integrity—of them there is nothing to say;
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Those broken by the changes of the times who lose their lifelong integrity—of them there is nothing to say;

sentences.zh: 因世變而意氣有所加者，亦私心也。”

translations.literal: but to let the changes of the times inflate one's spirit—that too is private feeling."
translations.idiomatic: but to let the changes of the times inflate one's spirit—that too is private feeling."

sentences.zh: 所為文有《大愚集》。

translations.literal: His writings were collected in the Dayu ji.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were collected in the Dayu ji.

sentences.zh: 祖儉從弟祖泰。

translations.literal: Zujian's younger cousin was Zutai.
translations.idiomatic: Zujian's younger cousin was Zutai.

sentences.zh: 祖泰。

translations.literal: Zutai.
translations.idiomatic: Zutai.

sentences.zh: 字泰然，夷簡六世孫，寓常之宜興。

translations.literal: Style name Tairan, sixth-generation descendant of Lü Yijian, residing at Yixing in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Style name Tairan, sixth-generation descendant of Lü Yijian, residing at Yixing in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性疏達，尚氣誼，學問該洽。

translations.literal: By nature open and broad-minded, he valued honor and friendship, and his learning was wide and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: By nature open and broad-minded, he valued honor and friendship, and his learning was wide and thorough.

sentences.zh: 遍遊江、淮，交當世知名士，得錢或分挈以去，無吝色。

translations.literal: He traveled throughout the Yangzi and Huai regions, befriending celebrated men of the age; when he got money he sometimes shared it and went on without a hint of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled throughout the Yangzi and Huai regions, befriending celebrated men of the age; when he got money he sometimes shared it and went on without a hint of reluctance.

sentences.zh: 飲酒至數鬥不醉，論世事無所忌諱，聞者或掩耳而走。

translations.literal: He could drink several dou without getting drunk; when he discussed current affairs he held nothing back, and some who heard him covered their ears and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink several dou without getting drunk; when he discussed current affairs he held nothing back, and some who heard him covered their ears and fled.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，祖儉以言事安置韶州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qingyuan reign, Zujian was settled at Shaozhou for memorializing on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingyuan reign, Zujian was settled at Shaozhou for memorializing on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 既移瑞州，祖泰徒步往省之，留月餘，語其友王深厚曰：“自吾兄之貶，諸人箝口。

translations.literal: After his transfer to Ruizhou, Zutai traveled on foot to visit him and stayed over a month, telling his friend Wang Shenhou: "Since my elder brother's banishment, everyone has silenced themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After his transfer to Ruizhou, Zutai traveled on foot to visit him and stayed over a month, telling his friend Wang Shenhou, "Since my elder brother's banishment, everyone has silenced themselves.

sentences.zh: 我雖無位，義必以言報國，當少須之，今未敢以累吾兄也。”

translations.literal: Though I hold no office, duty requires me to speak for the realm. I must wait a little—I dare not involve my brother yet."
translations.idiomatic: Though I hold no office, duty requires me to speak for the realm. I must wait a little—I dare not involve my brother yet."

sentences.zh: 及祖儉沒貶所，嘉泰元年，周必大降少保致仕，祖泰憤之，乃詣登聞鼓院上書，論侂胄有無君之心，請誅之以防禍亂。

translations.literal: When Zujian died in exile, in the first year of Jiatai Zhou Bida was demoted to Junior Guardian and retired, Zutai in anger went to the Memorial Drum Court and submitted a memorial accusing Tuozhou of disloyalty and asking that he be executed to guard against calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Zujian died in exile, in the first year of Jiatai Zhou Bida was demoted to Junior Guardian and retired; Zutai, in anger, went to the Memorial Drum Court and submitted a memorial accusing Tuozhou of disloyalty and asking that he be executed to guard against calamity.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：“道學，自古所恃以為國也。

translations.literal: The gist read: "The Way and learning—since antiquity the state has relied upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The gist read, "The Way and learning—since antiquity the state has relied upon them.

sentences.zh: 丞相汝愚，今之有大勳勞者也。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Ruyu is a man of great merit in our time.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Ruyu is a man of great merit in our time.

sentences.zh: 立偽學之禁，逐汝愚之黨，是將空陛下之國，而陛下不知悟邪？

translations.literal: To establish a ban on 'false learning' and drive out Ruyu's faction is to empty Your Majesty's realm—yet does Your Majesty not see it?
translations.idiomatic: To establish a ban on 'false learning' and drive out Ruyu's faction is to empty Your Majesty's realm—yet does Your Majesty not see it?

sentences.zh: 陳自強，侂胄童孺之師，躐致宰輔。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang, Tuozhou's childhood tutor, leaped straight to the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang, Tuozhou's childhood tutor, leaped straight to the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 陛下舊學之臣，若彭龜年等，今安在邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's old study companions, such as Peng Guinian—where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's old study companions, such as Peng Guinian—where are they now?

sentences.zh: 蘇師旦，平江之史胥，以潛邸而得節鉞；

translations.literal: Su Shidan, a clerk-scribe from Pingjiang, obtained military command through connection with the Hidden Residence;
translations.idiomatic: Su Shidan, a clerk-scribe from Pingjiang, obtained military command through connection with the Hidden Residence;

sentences.zh: 周筠，韓氏之廝役，以皇后親屬得大官。

translations.literal: Zhou Yun, a menial of the Han clan, gained high office through kinship with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yun, a menial of the Han clan, gained high office through kinship with the empress.

sentences.zh: 不識陛下在潛邸時果識師旦乎？

translations.literal: Did Your Majesty really know Shidan when you were at the Hidden Residence?
translations.idiomatic: Did Your Majesty really know Shidan when you were at the Hidden Residence?

sentences.zh: 椒房之親果有筠乎？

translations.literal: Did the empress's kin truly include Yun?
translations.idiomatic: Did the empress's kin truly include Yun?

sentences.zh: 凡侂胄之徒，自尊大而卑朝廷，一至於此也！

translations.literal: In every way Tuozhou's faction exalts itself and belittles the court—matters have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: In every way Tuozhou's faction exalts itself and belittles the court—matters have come to this!

sentences.zh: 願亟誅侂胄及師旦、周筠，而罷逐自強之徒。

translations.literal: I beg that Tuozhou, Shidan, and Zhou Yun be swiftly put to death, and that Ziqiang and his ilk be dismissed and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Tuozhou, Shidan, and Zhou Yun be swiftly put to death, and that Ziqiang and his ilk be dismissed and driven out.

sentences.zh: 獨周必大可用，宜以代之，不然，事將不測。”

translations.literal: Zhou Bida alone is fit for service and should replace them; otherwise events will become unpredictable."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida alone is fit for service and should replace them; otherwise events will become unpredictable."

sentences.zh: 書出，中外大駭。

translations.literal: When the memorial appeared, court and countryside alike were deeply shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial appeared, court and countryside alike were deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 有旨：“呂祖泰挾私上書，語言狂妄，拘管連州。”

translations.literal: An edict: "Lü Zutai submitted a memorial out of private motive with reckless language; he is to be detained and supervised at Lian Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down: "Lü Zutai submitted a memorial out of private motive with reckless language; he is to be detained and supervised at Lian Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫程鬆與祖泰狎友，懼曰：“人知我素與遊，其謂預聞乎？”

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Cheng Song, an intimate friend of Zutai, feared and said: "People know I have long associated with him—will they think I knew in advance?"
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Officer Cheng Song, an intimate friend of Zutai, feared and said, "People know I have long associated with him—will they think I knew in advance?"

sentences.zh: 乃獨奏言：“祖泰有當誅之罪，且其上書必有教之者，今縱不殺，猶當杖黥竄遠方。”

translations.literal: He then alone memorialized: "Zutai's crime deserves death, and there must have been someone who taught him to write that memorial; even if he is not killed now, he should still be flogged, tattooed, and exiled to a distant place."
translations.idiomatic: He then alone memorialized, "Zutai's crime deserves death, and there must have been someone who taught him to write that memorial; even if he is not killed now, he should still be flogged, tattooed, and exiled to a distant place."

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史陳讜亦以為言。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Chen Tan also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Censor Chen Tan also spoke to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 乃杖之百，配欽州牢城收管。

translations.literal: He was flogged one hundred strokes and assigned to garrison detention at Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was flogged one hundred strokes and assigned to garrison detention at Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史林采言偽習之成，造端自必大，故有少保之命。

translations.literal: Earlier, Supervising Censor Lin Cai had said the formation of 'false learning' originated with Bida, and so came the order making him Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Supervising Censor Lin Cai had said the formation of 'false learning' originated with Bida, and so came the order making him Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 祖泰知必死，冀以身悟朝廷，無懼色。

translations.literal: Zutai knew he must die; he hoped to awaken the court through his own body, and showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zutai knew he must die; he hoped to awaken the court through his own body, and showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 既至府廷，尹為好語誘之曰：“誰教汝共為章？

translations.literal: When he reached the prefectural hall, the prefect tried to coax him with kind words: "Who taught you to write that memorial together?
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the prefectural hall, the prefect tried to coax him with kind words: "Who taught you to write that memorial together?

sentences.zh: 汝試言之，吾且寬汝。”

translations.literal: Tell me, and I shall lighten your punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, and I shall lighten your punishment."

sentences.zh: 祖泰笑曰：“公何問之愚也。

translations.literal: Zutai laughed and said: "Sir, how foolish to ask such a question!
translations.idiomatic: Zutai laughed and said, "Sir, how foolish to ask such a question!

sentences.zh: 吾固知必死，而可受教於人，且與人議之乎？”

translations.literal: I knew from the start I must die—how could I accept instruction from another, or even discuss it with anyone?"
translations.idiomatic: I knew from the start I must die—how could I accept instruction from another, or even discuss it with anyone?"

sentences.zh: 尹曰：“汝病風喪心邪？”

translations.literal: The prefect said: "Are you mad with wind sickness and have lost your mind?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect said, "Are you mad with wind sickness and have lost your mind?"

sentences.zh: 祖泰曰：“以吾觀之，若今之附韓氏得美官者，乃病風喪心耳。”

translations.literal: Zutai said: "As I see it, those who now attach themselves to the Han clan and win fine posts—they are the ones mad with wind sickness and bereft of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zutai said, "As I see it, those who now attach themselves to the Han clan and win fine posts—they are the ones mad with wind sickness and bereft of mind.

sentences.zh: 祖泰既貶，道出潭州，錢文子為醴陵令，私贐其行。

translations.literal: After Zutai was banished, passing through Tan Prefecture on the road, Qian Wenzi was magistrate of Liling and privately supplied his journey.
translations.idiomatic: After Zutai was banished, passing through Tan Prefecture on the road, Qian Wenzi was magistrate of Liling and privately supplied his journey.

sentences.zh: 侂胄使人跡其所在，祖泰乃匿襄、郢間。

translations.literal: Tuozhou sent men to track his whereabouts; Zutai then hid between Xiang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou sent men to track his whereabouts; Zutai then hid between Xiang and Ying.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，朝廷訪得祖泰所在，詔雪其冤，特補上州文學，改授迪功郎、監南嶽廟。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, the court found where Zutai was, issued an edict clearing his wrong, specially appointed him Erudite of an upper prefecture, and reappointed him as Diligent Officer and keeper of the Southern Marchmount Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou was executed, the court found where Zutai was, issued an edict clearing his wrong, specially appointed him Erudite of an upper prefecture, and reappointed him as Diligent Officer and keeper of the Southern Marchmount Temple.

sentences.zh: 喪母無以葬，至都謀於諸公，得寒疾，索紙書曰：“吾與吾兄共攻權臣，今權臣誅，吾死不憾。

translations.literal: After his mother died he had no means to bury her; he went to the capital to seek help from the grandees, took a chill, asked for paper and wrote: "My elder brother and I alike assailed the powerful minister; now that minister is dead, I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he had no means to bury her; he went to the capital to seek help from the grandees, took a chill, asked for paper and wrote, "My elder brother and I alike assailed the powerful minister; now that minister is dead, I die without regret.

sentences.zh: 獨吾生還無以報國，且未能葬吾母，為可憾耳。”

translations.literal: Only that I have returned alive yet done nothing to serve the realm, and have been unable to bury my mother—that alone is regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: Only that I have returned alive yet done nothing to serve the realm, and have been unable to bury my mother—that alone is regrettable."

sentences.zh: 乃卒。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 尹王柟為具棺斂歸葬焉。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Shan provided a coffin, prepared his remains, and sent them home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Shan provided a coffin, prepared his remains, and sent them home for burial.

sentences.zh: 楊宏中字充甫，福州人。

translations.literal: Yang Hongzhong, style name Chongfu, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hongzhong, style name Chongfu, was a man of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弱冠補國子生。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he entered the Imperial Academy as a student.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he entered the Imperial Academy as a student.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，光宗以疾不能執喪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Guangzong was ill and unable to perform mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Guangzong was ill and unable to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 時趙汝愚知樞密院，奏請太皇太后迎立寧宗於嘉邸，以成喪禮，朝野晏然。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Ruyu directed the Bureau of Military Affairs and memorialized asking the Grand Empress Dowager to welcome Ningzong from the Jia Residence to take the throne and complete the mourning rites; court and countryside alike were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Ruyu directed the Bureau of Military Affairs and memorialized asking the Grand Empress Dowager to welcome Ningzong from the Jia Residence to take the throne and complete the mourning rites; court and countryside alike were at peace.

sentences.zh: 遂命汝愚為右丞相，登進耆德及一時知名之士，有意慶曆、元祐之治。

translations.literal: Ruyu was then made chief minister on the right, elevated venerable elders and celebrated men of the age, with an eye toward governance like the Qingli and Yuanyou eras.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu was then made chief minister on the right, elevated venerable elders and celebrated men of the age, with an eye toward governance like the Qingli and Yuanyou eras.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄竊弄國柄，引將作監李沐為右正言，首論罷汝愚，中丞何澹、御史胡紱章繼上，竄汝愚永州。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou secretly wielded state power, brought in Li Mu from the Directorate of Palace Buildings as Right Remonstrance Adviser, who first memorialized to dismiss Ruyu; Censor-in-chief He Dan and Censor Hu Hong and others followed, and Ruyu was banished to Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou secretly wielded state power, brought in Li Mu from the Directorate of Palace Buildings as Right Remonstrance Adviser, who first memorialized to dismiss Ruyu; Censor-in-chief He Dan and Censor Hu Hong and others followed, and Ruyu was banished to Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒李祥、博士楊簡連疏救爭，俱被斥。

translations.literal: Academy Libationer Li Xiang and Erudite Yang Jian submitted successive memorials pleading in protest—both were driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Academy Libationer Li Xiang and Erudite Yang Jian submitted successive memorials pleading in protest—both were driven out.

sentences.zh: 宏中曰：“師儒能辨大臣之冤，而諸生不能留師儒之去，於誼安乎？”

translations.literal: Hongzhong said: "Our teachers can discern the injustice done to a great minister—yet we students cannot keep our teachers from leaving. Where is the propriety in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhong said, "Our teachers can discern the injustice done to a great minister—yet we students cannot keep our teachers from leaving. Where is the propriety in that?"

sentences.zh: 眾莫應，獨林仲麟、徐範、張衟、蔣傅、周端朝五人願預其議。

translations.literal: The crowd did not answer; only Lin Zhonglin, Xu Fan, Zhang Yu, Jiang Fu, and Zhou Duanchao—five men—wished to join the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd did not answer; only Lin Zhonglin, Xu Fan, Zhang Yu, Jiang Fu, and Zhou Duanchao—five men—wished to join the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 遂上書曰：

translations.literal: They then submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: They then submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 自古國家禍亂之由，初非一道，惟小人中傷君子，其禍尤慘。

translations.literal: Since antiquity the causes of a state's ruin and turmoil have never been single—but when petty men wound worthy men, the calamity is especially grievous.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the causes of a state's ruin and turmoil have never been single—but when petty men wound worthy men, the calamity is especially grievous.

sentences.zh: 君子登庸，杜絕邪枉，要其處心實在於愛君憂國。

translations.literal: When worthy men hold office they shut out the crooked; at bottom their hearts lie in loving the ruler and grieving for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men hold office they shut out the crooked; at bottom their hearts lie in loving the ruler and grieving for the state.

sentences.zh: 小人得誌，仇視正人，必欲空其朋類，然後可以肆行而無忌。

translations.literal: When petty men get their way they hate the upright, empty out their allies, and only then can act without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men get their way they hate the upright, empty out their allies, and only then can act without restraint.

sentences.zh: 於是人主孤立，而社稷危矣。

translations.literal: Then the ruler stands alone, and the altars of soil and grain are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler stands alone, and the altars of soil and grain are in peril.

sentences.zh: 黨錮敞漢，朋黨亂唐，大率由此。

translations.literal: The faction proscriptions ruined Han; cliques threw Tang into chaos—mostly from this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The faction proscriptions ruined Han; cliques threw Tang into chaos—mostly from this pattern.

sentences.zh: 元祐以來，邪正交攻，卒成靖康之變，臣子所不忍言，而陛下所不忍聞也。

translations.literal: From Yuanyou onward orthodox and heterodox attacked each other, until at last came the Jingkang catastrophe—what subjects cannot bear to speak of, and what Your Majesty cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanyou onward orthodox and heterodox attacked each other, until at last came the Jingkang catastrophe—what subjects cannot bear to speak of, and what Your Majesty cannot bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見近者諫臣李沐論前宰相趙汝愚數談夢兆，擅權植黨，將不利於陛下。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that recently Remonstrance Adviser Li Mu spoke of former chief minister Zhao Ruyu discussing dream omens repeatedly, monopolizing power and building factions, with intent harmful to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that recently Remonstrance Adviser Li Mu spoke of former chief minister Zhao Ruyu discussing dream omens repeatedly, monopolizing power and building factions, with intent harmful to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 以此加誣，實不其然。

translations.literal: To add such slander on top of it is in truth not so.
translations.idiomatic: To heap such false charges upon him is simply untrue.

sentences.zh: 汝愚乞去，中外谘憤，而言者以為父老歡呼，蒙蔽天聽，一至於此。

translations.literal: Ruyu begged to leave office; court and countryside alike were indignant and aggrieved, yet the remonstrators claimed the elders were cheering and had deceived the imperial ear—matters had come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu begged to resign; court and countryside seethed with indignation, yet the remonstrators claimed the common people were cheering and had deceived the throne—things had sunk to this.

sentences.zh: 章穎力辨其非，首遭斥逐，聞者已駭；

translations.literal: Zhang Ying forcefully argued that this was wrong and was the first to be driven out; those who heard it were already shaken;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying forcefully rebutted the charge and was the first expelled; all who heard of it were shaken;

sentences.zh: 既而祭酒李祥、博士楊簡相繼抗論，毅然求去，告假幾月，善類皇皇。

translations.literal: then the Erudite Li Xiang and the Erudite Yang Jian in succession remonstrated, resolutely sought to leave, took leave for several months, and worthy men were in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: then the Erudite Li Xiang and the Erudite Yang Jian remonstrated in turn, resolutely resigned, took leave for months, and men of integrity grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 一旦有外補之命，言者惡其扶植正論，極力牴排，同日報罷，六館之士為之憤惋涕泣。

translations.literal: Once there came orders for outside appointments, the remonstrators hated that they upheld upright discourse, strove with all their might to oppose them, and on the same day reported their dismissal; the students of the Six Halls wept and grieved in anger for them.
translations.idiomatic: When outside appointments were issued, the remonstrators resented their support of upright opinion and pressed hard for their removal; dismissed the same day, the students of the Six Halls wept in outrage.

sentences.zh: 今李沐自知邪正之不兩立，而公議之不直己也，乃欲盡去正人以便其私，於是托朋黨以罔陛下之聽。

translations.literal: Now Li Mu, knowing that the upright and the crooked cannot stand together and that public opinion does not favor him, wished to remove all upright men to ease his private ends; he therefore invoked factionalism to deceive Your Majesty's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu, knowing that good and evil cannot coexist and that public opinion condemned him, sought to purge every upright man for his private advantage and invoked the charge of faction to mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣謂二人之去若未足惜，殆恐君子小人消長之機於此一判，則靖康已然之監，豈堪復見於今日邪？

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if the departure of these two men were not yet worth regretting, one would still fear that the turning point in the waxing and waning of worthy men and petty men is decided here; the lesson of the Jingkang disaster is already before us—can we bear to see it again today?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the loss of these two men were not yet grave in itself, I fear the decisive turn in the struggle between worthy men and petty men comes here; the warning of Jingkang already stands before us—can we endure to see it repeated?

sentences.zh: 陛下厲精圖政，方將正三綱以維人心，采群議以定國是，遽聽奸回，概疑善類，此臣等之所未諭也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is exerting yourself to reform governance and is just about to set right the Three Bonds to preserve the hearts of the people and gather many opinions to fix the national course; yet you suddenly heed treacherous men and broadly suspect the good—this is what we your servants cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is striving to reform the realm, about to restore the Three Bonds and gather counsel to settle the nation's course—yet you suddenly heed traitors and suspect the good wholesale. We cannot fathom this.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下鑒漢、唐之禍，懲靖康之變，精加宸慮，特奮睿斷。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to reflect on the disasters of Han and Tang, take warning from the Jingkang upheaval, refine your imperial deliberation, and specially rouse your sage decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to heed the catastrophes of Han and Tang, take warning from Jingkang, sharpen your imperial judgment, and act with resolute wisdom.

sentences.zh: 念汝愚之忠勤，察祥簡之非黨，灼李沐之回邪，明示好惡，旌別淑慝，竄李沐以謝天下，還祥、簡以收士心，臣雖身膏鼎鑊，實所不辭。

translations.literal: Recall Ruyu's loyalty and diligence, discern that Xiang and Jian are no faction, mark clearly Li Mu's perversity and wickedness, openly show what you favor and hate, distinguish the good from the evil, banish Li Mu to appease the realm, restore Xiang and Jian to win the hearts of scholars—even if your servant's body is rendered in the cauldron and cauldron, he will not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Remember Ruyu's loyal service, see that Xiang and Jian are no faction, expose Li Mu's depravity, declare your likes and dislikes, separate good from evil, banish Li Mu to appease the realm, restore Xiang and Jian to win scholars' hearts—even if I am boiled alive, I shall not refuse.

sentences.zh: 書奏不報，則繳副封於台諫、侍從。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted and received no reply, they then turned in a sealed copy to the remonstrance and censorial offices and the attendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial went unanswered, they submitted a sealed copy to the remonstrance and censorial bureaus and the attendant officials.

sentences.zh: 侂胄大怒，坐以不合上書之罪，六人皆編置，以宏中為首，將竄之嶺南。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly enraged, convicted them on the charge of improper memorial submission, and all six were banished to distant posts, with Hongzhong listed first; they were to be exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou flew into a rage, convicted them of improper memorial submission, and banished all six—Hongzhong named first—to distant posts, intending exile to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人鄧馹上書救之，不聽。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Drafter Deng Yi submitted a memorial to save them; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Drafter Deng Yi memorialized in their defense; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 右丞相餘端禮拜於榻前至數十，丐免遠徙。

translations.literal: The chief minister on the right Yu Duanli kowtowed before the couch dozens of times, begging that they be spared distant exile.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yu Duanli kowtowed before the throne dozens of times, begging that they be spared distant exile.

sentences.zh: 上惻然許之，乃送太平州編管。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved to pity, assented, and they were sent to Taiping Prefecture under registered banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, the emperor assented and sent them to registered banishment in Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天下號為“六君子”。

translations.literal: The realm called them the "Six Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: All the realm hailed them as the "Six Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 明年，移福州聽讀。

translations.literal: The next year they were transferred to Fuzhou to hear lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they were transferred to Fuzhou to attend lectures.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，寧宗幸學，持旨放還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai, when Emperor Ningzong visited the academy, an edict was issued for their release and return.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai 3, when Emperor Ningzong visited the Imperial Academy, an edict ordered their release and return.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，宏中登進士第，教授南劍州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi, Hongzhong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed instructor in Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 1, Hongzhong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed instructor in Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太守餘嶸，故相端禮子，與之相得甚歡。

translations.literal: The prefect Yu Zheng, son of the former chief minister Duanli, and he got on together very happily.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Yu Zheng, son of the former chief minister Duanli, became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，先以言得罪者悉加褒錄。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, all who had earlier been punished for their words were commended and restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou's execution, all who had been punished for speaking out were commended and restored.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，特遷宏中一秩，亦不拜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, Hongzhong was specially promoted one rank, yet he still did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 1, Hongzhong was specially promoted one rank, but he still declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 六年，以嶸與汪逵、趙彥橚薦，授戶部架閣，俄遷太學正。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on recommendation by Zheng together with Wang Kui and Zhao Yansu, he was appointed Archivist in the Ministry of Revenue, and soon after was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, recommended by Zheng, Wang Kui, and Zhao Yansu, he was made Archivist in the Ministry of Revenue and soon became Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 八年夏旱，上封事，指切無隱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, during a summer drought, he submitted a sealed memorial, criticizing directly and concealing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, during a summer drought, he submitted a sealed memorial, speaking bluntly and hiding nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷武學博士，改宣教郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Military Academy and changed to Instructor Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the Military Academy and promoted to Instructor Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時諫官應武論一學官，宏中季試策士及其故，武聞而銜之。

translations.literal: At that time the remonstrance official Ying Wu criticized a certain academy officer; Hongzhong, in the seasonal examination, questioned the candidates about the reason, and Wu, hearing of it, bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance official Ying Wu had criticized an academy officer; Hongzhong raised the matter in a seasonal examination of the students, and Wu, hearing of it, nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 秋戊祀武成王，祭酒行事。

translations.literal: In autumn on the wu day the Martial Accomplishment King was sacrificed to, and the Erudite performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, on the wu day, the sacrifice to the Martial Accomplishment King was performed by the Erudite.

sentences.zh: 故事，博士攝亞獻，至是不命宏中，宏中白於祭酒。

translations.literal: By precedent the Erudite served as deputy presenter; this time Hongzhong was not ordered to do so, and Hongzhong reported this to the Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Erudite served as deputy presenter; this time Hongzhong was not appointed, and he reported the matter to the Erudite.

sentences.zh: 於是武劾宏中與同列競，且謂其激矯不自愛，遂通判潭州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu impeached Hongzhong for competing with his colleagues and further said he was contentious and did not cherish himself, and so Hongzhong was made Vice Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then impeached Hongzhong for contending with his colleagues and for reckless contentiousness, and had him made Vice Prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以親老請祠，差知武岡軍，未受卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Because his parents were old he requested a sinecure; he was appointed prefect of Wugang Army, but before he could take up the post he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Citing aged parents, he sought a temple post; he was appointed prefect of Wugang Army but died before taking office, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 端朝字子靜，嘉定三年試禮部第一，終刑部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: Duanchao, style name Zijing, placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination in the third year of Jiading, and ended as Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Duanchao, style name Zijing, ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination in Jiading 3 and rose to Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 衟字用叟，以父任補官，有二子，與端朝同登進士第。

translations.literal: Yu, style name Yongsou, entered office through his father's privilege; he had two sons who passed the jinshi examination together with Duanchao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, style name Yongsou, entered office by his father's privilege; he had two sons who passed the jinshi together with Duanchao.

sentences.zh: 仲麟字景仲，傅字象夫，久居學校，忠鯁有聞，鹹以不偶死。

translations.literal: Zhonglin, style name Jingzhong; Fu, style name Xiangfu—long resident in the schools, known for loyal bluntness; all died without attaining their due.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglin, style name Jingzhong, and Fu, style name Xiangfu, had long lived in the academies, famed for blunt loyalty; all died without receiving their due reward.

sentences.zh: 範自有傳。

translations.literal: Fan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fan has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 華嶽，字子西，為武學生，輕財好俠。

translations.literal: Hua Yue, style name Zixi, was a student of the Military Academy, light with wealth and fond of chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yue, style name Zixi, was a student of the Military Academy—generous with his wealth and fond of bold deeds.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄當國，嶽上書曰：

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held the state, Yue submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou dominated the state, Yue submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 旬月以來，都城士民彷徨四顧，若將喪其室家；

translations.literal: For a month now the gentry and common people of the capital have wandered in alarm, looking about as if they were about to lose their homes and families;
translations.idiomatic: For a month now the people of the capital have wandered in dread, glancing about as though their homes and families were already lost;

sentences.zh: 諸軍妻子隱哭含悲，若將驅之水火。

translations.literal: the wives and children of the various armies weep in hidden grief, as if they were about to be driven into fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers' wives and children weep in hidden grief, as though about to be cast into fire and water.

sentences.zh: 闤闠籍籍，欲語復噤，駭於傳聞，莫曉所謂。

translations.literal: In the markets there is a buzz of talk; people wish to speak yet fall silent again, terrified by rumor, not knowing what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Markets murmur with rumor; people want to speak yet fall silent, terrified by what they hear, unable to grasp what it means.

sentences.zh: 臣徐考之，則侍衛之兵日夜潛發，樞機之遞星火交馳，戎作之役倍於平時，郵傳之程兼於疇昔，乃知陛下將有事於北征也。

translations.literal: Your servant has slowly examined the matter and finds that the palace guard troops are being secretly dispatched day and night, dispatches from the Bureau of Military Affairs fly like sparks, military labor is double the usual, and courier schedules are heavier than before—thus one knows Your Majesty is about to undertake a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On careful inquiry I find palace guards dispatched secretly day and night, military dispatches flying like sparks, corvée doubled, courier schedules doubled—Your Majesty is preparing a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 侂胄以後族之親，位居極品，專執權柄，公取賄賂；

translations.literal: Tuozhou, by kinship to the empress dowager's clan, occupies the highest rank, monopolizes power, and openly takes bribes;
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou, kin to the empress dowager's clan, holds the highest rank, monopolizes power, and openly accepts bribes;

sentences.zh: 畜養無籍吏仆，委以腹心，賣名器，私爵賞，睥睨神器，窺覘宗社，日益炎炎，不敢向爾。

translations.literal: he keeps unregistered clerks and servants, entrusts them as his intimates, sells offices and titles, grants honors in private, looks askance at the imperial regalia, and peeps at the altars of state—day by day more overbearing, and one dares not face it.
translations.idiomatic: he keeps unregistered clerks and servants as his intimates, sells offices and honors in private, covets the throne, and watches the altars of state—growing bolder daily, beyond what one dares confront.

sentences.zh: 此外患之居吾腹心者也。

translations.literal: This is the external peril seated in our heart.
translations.idiomatic: This is the external peril lodged in our very heart.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有以庸瑣之資，請姻師旦，驟入政府者；

translations.literal: Among court ministers there are those of mediocre and petty talent who sought marriage with Shidan and suddenly entered the chief council;
translations.idiomatic: Some court ministers of mediocre talent sought marriage ties with Shidan and suddenly entered the chief council;

sentences.zh: 有以諛佞之資，附阿侂胄，致身顯貴者。

translations.literal: there are those of flattery and sycophancy who attached themselves to Tuozhou and rose to wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: others of flattery and sycophancy clung to Tuozhou and rose to wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 陳自強老不知恥，貪不知止，私植黨與，陰結門第，凡見諸行事，惟知侂胄，不知君父。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang is old yet knows no shame, greedy and knowing no stop; he privately plants factions and secretly binds himself to great houses—in all that appears in his conduct he knows only Tuozhou and not ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang, old yet shameless, greedy without limit, secretly builds factions and binds himself to great houses—in all he does he knows only Tuozhou, not his ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 此外患之居吾股肱者也。

translations.literal: This is the external peril seated in our arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: This is the external peril lodged in our arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 爽、奕、汝翼諸李之貪懦無謀，倪、僎、倬、杲諸郭之膏粱無用，諸吳之恃寵專僭，諸彭之庸孱不肖；

translations.literal: Among the Lis—Shuang, Yi, and Ruyi—are greed and cowardice without counsel; among the Guos—Ni, Zhuan, Zhuo, and Gao—are pampered sons without use; among the Wus are those who rely on favor and usurp privilege; among the Pengs are mediocrity and feebleness unworthy of their posts;
translations.idiomatic: The Lis—Shuang, Yi, and Ruyi—are greedy cowards without counsel; the Guos—Ni, Zhuan, Zhuo, and Gao—are useless pampered sons; the Wus trade on favor and exceed their rank; the Pengs are mediocrities unfit for office;

sentences.zh: 皇甫斌、魏友諒、毛致通、秦世輔之雕瘵軍心、瘡痍士氣，以致陳孝慶、夏興祖、商榮、田俊邁之徒，皆以一卒之材，各得把麾專製，平日剜膏刻血，包苴侂胄，以致通顯，饑寒之士鹹願食其肉而不可得。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bin, Wei Youliang, Mao Zhitong, and Qin Shifu have wasted the army's heart and scarred its morale, so that men like Chen Xiaoqing, Xia Xingzu, Shang Rong, and Tian Junmai—all with the talent of a single soldier—each hold command and act on their own; in ordinary times they flayed the people and bribed Tuozhou to reach prominence, while starving scholars all wished to eat their flesh yet could not.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bin, Wei Youliang, Mao Zhitong, and Qin Shifu have drained the army's spirit and scarred its morale, so that men like Chen Xiaoqing, Xia Xingzu, Shang Rong, and Tian Junmai—each no better than a common soldier—hold independent command; they flayed the people and bribed Tuozhou for rank, while hungry scholars longed to devour them and could not.

sentences.zh: 萬一陛下付以大事，彼之首領自不可保，奚暇為陛下計哉？

translations.literal: If by chance Your Majesty should entrust them with great affairs, their own heads could not be preserved—how would they have leisure to plan for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty entrust them with great affairs, they could not save their own heads—much less plan for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此外患之居吾爪牙者也。

translations.literal: This is the external peril seated in our claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: This is the external peril lodged in our claws and teeth.

sentences.zh: 程鬆之納妾求知，或以售妹入府，或以獻妻入閣，魯

translations.literal: Cheng Song took concubines seeking advancement; some sold their sisters to enter his mansion, some offered their wives to enter the chief counselor's office; Lu
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song took concubines to curry favor; some sold sisters to enter his mansion, some offered wives to enter the Cabinet; Lu

sentences.zh: 之貢子為郎，富宮之庸駑充位。

translations.literal: offered his son as tribute to become a court gentleman; mediocrity such as Fu Tong filled the posts.
translations.idiomatic: offered his son as tribute to gain a court post; worthless men like Fu Tong filled the offices.

sentences.zh: 此外患之居吾耳目者也。

translations.literal: This is the external peril seated in our ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: This is the external peril lodged in our ears and eyes.

sentences.zh: 蘇師旦以穢吏冒節鉞，牙儈名爵；

translations.literal: Su Shidan, a foul clerk, usurped the seal and battle-axe; a broker in offices and titles;
translations.idiomatic: Su Shidan, a foul clerk, usurped the seal and battle-axe and brokered offices and titles;

sentences.zh: 周筠以隸卒冒戎鈐，市易將相。

translations.literal: Zhou Yun, a menial soldier, usurped military authority and traded in generals and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yun, a menial soldier, usurped military authority and traded in generals and chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 此外患之扼吾咽喉者也。

translations.literal: This is the external peril that chokes our throat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the external peril throttling our throat.

sentences.zh: 彼之所謂外患者實未足憂，而此之外患蓋已周吾一身之間矣。

translations.literal: The so-called external peril of which they speak is in truth not worth worrying over; yet this external peril has already encircled our entire person.
translations.idiomatic: The external enemies they speak of are hardly worth fearing; yet this peril already surrounds us on every side.

sentences.zh: “禮樂征伐，自天子出”。

translations.literal: "Rites, music, campaigns, and punishments issue from the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "Rites, music, campaigns, and punishments issue from the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 所貴乎中國者，皆聽命於陛下也。

translations.literal: What is precious in the Middle Kingdom is that all obey the commands of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The glory of the Middle Kingdom is that all obey Your Majesty's command.

sentences.zh: 今也與奪之命、黜陟之權，又不出於陛下，而出於侂胄。

translations.literal: Now the power to grant and revoke, to dismiss and promote, no longer issues from Your Majesty but from Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now the power to appoint, dismiss, and promote no longer rests with Your Majesty but with Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 是吾有二中國也。

translations.literal: Thus we have two Middle Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we have two Middle Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 命又不出於侂胄，而出於蘇師旦、周筠。

translations.literal: Commands no longer issue from Tuozhou but from Su Shidan and Zhou Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Commands no longer issue even from Tuozhou but from Su Shidan and Zhou Yun.

sentences.zh: 是吾有三中國也。

translations.literal: Thus we have three Middle Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we have three Middle Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 女真以區區之地，猶能逼我淮、漢，曾謂外患之居吾腹心、股肱、耳目、爪牙及吾咽喉，而不馮陵吾之宗廟社稷乎？

translations.literal: The Jurchen, with their tiny territory, can still press us on the Huai and Han—can one say that with external peril seated in our heart, arms, ears, claws, and throat, they will not overrun our altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen, from a tiny domain, still press us on the Huai and Han—while peril sits in our heart, limbs, ears, claws, and throat, will they not overrun our altars of state?

sentences.zh: 曾謂一家之中自為秦、越，一舟之中自為敵國，而能製遠人乎？

translations.literal: Can one say that within one household men become Qin and Yue to one another, or within one boat they become enemy states, and yet still control distant peoples?
translations.idiomatic: Can a household divided like Qin and Yue, or a boat whose passengers are enemy states, still command distant peoples?

sentences.zh: 比年軍皆掊克，而士卒自仇其將佐；

translations.literal: In recent years the armies have all been squeezed dry, and the soldiers themselves hate their commanders;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years armies have been squeezed dry, and soldiers hate their own officers;

sentences.zh: 民皆侵漁，而百姓自畔其守令，家自為戰。

translations.literal: the people have all been plundered, and the common folk themselves turn against their prefects and magistrates—each household fights on its own.
translations.idiomatic: officials plunder the people, and common folk turn against their magistrates—each household fights alone.

sentences.zh: 此又啟吾中國億萬之仇敵也。

translations.literal: This again opens up tens of millions of enemies within our Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: This again raises tens of millions of enemies within our realm.

sentences.zh: 今不務去吾腹心、股肱、爪牙、耳目、咽喉與夫億萬之仇敵，而欲空國之師，竭國之財，而與遠人相從於血刃相塗之地，顧不外用其心歟？

translations.literal: Now, instead of striving to remove the peril in our heart, arms, claws, ears, throat, and those tens of millions of enemies, you wish to empty the state's armies and exhaust the state's wealth and follow distant men to a place where blades are smeared with blood—is this not using your heart on external matters?
translations.idiomatic: Instead of removing the peril in our heart, limbs, claws, senses, throat, and those countless internal enemies, you would empty the armies and treasury to follow distant foes into slaughter—is this not misplacing your concern entirely?

sentences.zh: 臣嚐推演兵書，自去歲上元甲子，五福太一初度吳分，四神直符對臨荊、楚，始擊蜚符旁臨甌、粵，青門直使交次於幽、冀，黑殺黃道正按於燕、趙。

translations.literal: Your servant has once deduced from military texts that from last year, the first year of the upper primordial jiazi cycle, the Five Blessings and Grand Unity first measured the Wu region; the Four Spirits and Direct Talismans faced Jing and Chu; the Initial Strike and Flying Talisman stood beside by Ou and Yue; the Blue Gate Direct Envoy alternated between You and Ji; the Black Killer and Yellow Way pressed directly on Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has read the military texts: since last year's upper primordial jiazi, the Five Blessings and Grand Unity first measured Wu; the Four Spirits faced Jing and Chu; the Initial Strike hovered over Ou and Yue; the Blue Gate Envoy crossed You and Ji; the Black Killer pressed Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 考之成法，主算最長，客算最短。

translations.literal: Examining the established method, the host's count is longest and the guest's count is shortest.
translations.idiomatic: By established method, the host's count is longest and the guest's shortest.

sentences.zh: 兵以先發為客，後發為主。

translations.literal: In warfare, he who strikes first is the guest; he who strikes later is the host.
translations.idiomatic: In war, he who strikes first is the guest; he who strikes later is the host.

sentences.zh: 自太歲乙丑至庚午六年之間，皆不利於先舉。

translations.literal: From the year yichou of the Grand Year through the six years to gengwu, all are unfavorable to striking first.
translations.idiomatic: From yichou through the six years to gengwu, all auguries disfavor striking first.

sentences.zh: 儻其畔盟犯義，撓我疆場，至於事不獲已，然後應之，則反主為客，猶曰庶幾。

translations.literal: If they break the alliance and violate righteousness and harass our borders, until matters leave us no choice and we then respond, then guest and host are reversed—one may still say it is tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: If they break the alliance, violate righteousness, and harass our borders, and we respond only when there is no choice, host and guest are reversed—yet that may still be borne.

sentences.zh: 萬一國家首事倡謀，則將帥內睽，士卒外畔，肝腦萬民，血刃千里。

translations.literal: If by chance the state takes the initiative and starts the plan, then generals will be at odds within and soldiers will rebel without; the livers and brains of the myriad people will be scattered and blades will redden the land for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: But if the state takes the initiative, generals will quarrel within and soldiers rebel without; the people's blood will soak the land for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 此天數之不利於先舉也。

translations.literal: This is Heaven's number being unfavorable to striking first.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven's verdict against striking first.

sentences.zh: 矧將帥庸愚，軍民怨懟，馬政不講，騎士不熟，豪傑不出，英雄不收，饋糧不豐，形便不固，山砦不修，堡壘不設，吾雖帶甲百萬，餫餉千里，而師出無功，不戰自敗。

translations.literal: Moreover the generals are mediocre and foolish, soldiers and people resent and complain, horse policy is not discussed, cavalry are unskilled, heroes are not brought forth, brave men are not gathered, provisions are not abundant, terrain is not secure, mountain stockades are not repaired, fortresses are not set up—though we may have a million armored men and supply lines a thousand li long, the army will march out without success and be defeated without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the generals are fools, soldiers and people resentful, horse policy neglected, cavalry unskilled, heroes ignored, provisions thin, terrain insecure, stockades unrepaired, fortresses unbuilt—though we field a million men and supply lines a thousand li long, the army will fail without victory and fall without battle.

sentences.zh: 此人事之不利於先舉也。

translations.literal: This is human affairs being unfavorable to striking first.
translations.idiomatic: This is human affairs arrayed against striking first.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下除吾一身之外患。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to remove the external peril within our person.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to remove the peril within our own body.

sentences.zh: 吾國中之外患既已除，然後公道開明，正人登用，法令自行，紀綱自正，豪傑自歸，英雄自附，侵疆自還，中原自復；

translations.literal: Once the external peril within our state is removed, then the public Way will open, upright men will be employed, laws will execute themselves, discipline will right itself, heroes will return of themselves, brave men will attach themselves, invaded borders will return of themselves, and the Central Plain will be restored of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Once internal peril is gone, the public Way will open, upright men will serve, laws and discipline will right themselves, heroes will rally, borders will return, and the Central Plain will be restored;

sentences.zh: 天下自底於和平，四海自躋於仁壽，何俟乎兵革哉？

translations.literal: the realm will naturally reach peace, the four seas will naturally ascend to benevolence and longevity—why wait upon arms?
translations.idiomatic: the realm will find peace, the four seas reach benevolence and longevity—why wait on war?

sentences.zh: 不然，則亂臣賊子毀冕裂冠，哦九錫隆恩之詩，恃貴不可侔之相，私妾內姬，陰臣將相，魚肉軍士，塗炭生靈，墜百世之遠圖，虧十廟之遺業。

translations.literal: Otherwise rebellious ministers and wicked sons will destroy the crown and rend the cap, intone poems of the Nine Bestowals' lofty grace, rely on a chief minister whose nobility none may match, keep concubines and inner consorts privately, hide ministers and generals in shadow, treat soldiers as meat on the chopping block and the people as charred in the cauldron, and fall from the far-sighted plan of a hundred generations and fail the inherited enterprise of the ten temples.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise traitors will tear the crown, chant the Nine Bestowals, lean on an unmatched chief minister, keep private concubines and hidden generals, devour soldiers and burn the people, and ruin the plan of a hundred generations and the legacy of the ten temples.

sentences.zh: 陛下此時雖欲不與之偕亡，則禍迫於身，權出於人，俯首待終，何臍可噬。

translations.literal: At that time, though Your Majesty may wish not to perish together with them, calamity will press upon your person, power will issue from others, and bowing your head you await the end—what navel can you bite?
translations.idiomatic: Then, though Your Majesty wish not to perish with them, calamity will close in, power will belong to others, and you will bow your head awaiting the end with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 事之未然，難以取信，臣願以身屬之廷尉，待其軍行用師，勞還奏凱，則梟臣之首風遞四方，以為天下欺君罔上者之戒。

translations.literal: Before the matter has happened it is hard to win belief; your servant wishes to deliver his person to the Court of Judicial Review, and when the army marches and returns in triumph with labor, then the traitor's head may be sent by courier to the four quarters as a warning to all under heaven who deceive the ruler and mislead their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Before events unfold, words are hard to trust; I offer my person to the Court of Judicial Review—if the army marches and returns in triumph, let the traitor's head be sent to the four quarters as a warning to all who deceive their ruler.

sentences.zh: 儻或幹戈相尋，敗亡相繼，強敵外攻，奸臣內畔，與臣所言盡相符契，然後令臣歸老田裏，永為不齒之民。

translations.literal: If instead arms follow one upon another, defeat and ruin succeed in turn, strong enemies attack from without and traitorous ministers rebel within, matching in every point what your servant has said, then let your servant return old to his fields and forever be a man not counted among the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: But if war follows war, defeat follows defeat, enemies attack without and traitors rebel within, matching all I have said, then let me retire to my fields and live out my days disgraced.

sentences.zh: 書奏，侂胄大怒，下大理，貶建寧圜土中。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Tuozhou was greatly enraged, sent him down to the Court of Judicial Review, and banished him to imprisonment in Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Tuozhou was enraged, had him tried, and banished him to imprisonment in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 郡守傅伯成憐之，命獄卒使出入毋係。

translations.literal: The prefect Fu Bocheng pitied him and ordered the jailers to let him come and go without binding.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Fu Bocheng pitied him and ordered the jailers not to bind him.

sentences.zh: 伯成去，又迕守李大異，復置獄。

translations.literal: When Bocheng left and Yue again offended the new prefect Li Dayi, he was again imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Bocheng left and Yue again offended the new prefect Li Dayi, he was imprisoned again.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，放還，復入學登第，為殿前司官屬，鬱不得誌。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, Yue was released and returned; he re-entered the academy, passed the examinations, and became an officer of the Palace Front Office, yet was depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou's execution Yue was released; he re-entered the academy, passed the examinations, and became an officer of the Palace Front Office, but remained frustrated and unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 謀去丞相史彌遠，事覺，下臨安獄。

translations.literal: He plotted to remove Chief Minister Shi Miyuan; the matter was discovered and he was sent down to the Lin'an jail.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to remove Chief Minister Shi Miyuan; discovered, he was sent to the Lin'an jail.

sentences.zh: 獄具，坐議大臣當死。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, he was convicted of plotting against a chief minister and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, he was convicted of plotting against a chief minister and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 寧宗知嶽名，欲生之，彌遠曰：“是欲殺臣者。”

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong knew Yue's name and wished to spare his life; Miyuan said, "This is the man who wished to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ningzong knew Yue's name and wished to spare him; Miyuan said, "This is the man who wanted me dead."

sentences.zh: 竟杖死東市。

translations.literal: In the end he was beaten to death in the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was beaten to death in the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 鄧若水，字平仲，隆州井研人。

translations.literal: Deng Ruoshui, style name Pingzhong, was a man of Jingyan in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ruoshui, style name Pingzhong, was a native of Jingyan in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，為文章有氣骨。

translations.literal: He thoroughly mastered the classics and histories, and his writing had bone and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories, and wrote with force and integrity.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，州縣莫敢抗，若水方為布衣，憤甚，將殺縣令，起兵討之。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, prefectures and counties dared not resist; Ruoshui was then a commoner, greatly angered, and planned to kill the magistrate and raise troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, prefectures and counties dared not resist; Ruoshui, then a commoner, was furious and planned to kill the magistrate and raise troops against him.

sentences.zh: 夜刲雞盟其仆曰：“ 我明日謁知縣，汝密懷刃以從，我顧汝，即殺之。”

translations.literal: At night he slaughtered a chicken and swore his servant to an oath, saying, "Tomorrow I shall call on the magistrate; you secretly carry a blade and follow me—when I look at you, kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: At night he slaughtered a chicken and bound his servant by oath: "Tomorrow I shall visit the magistrate; secretly carry a blade and follow me—when I glance at you, strike him down."

sentences.zh: 仆佯許諾，至期三顧不發。

translations.literal: The servant feigned assent; when the day came he was thrice looked at yet did not act.
translations.idiomatic: The servant feigned assent; when the day came Ruoshui looked back three times, yet he did not strike.

sentences.zh: 歸責其仆以背盟，仆曰：“平人尚不可殺，況知縣乎？

translations.literal: Returning home he reproached his servant for breaking the oath; the servant said, "Even an ordinary man may not be killed—how much less a magistrate?
translations.idiomatic: Home again, he rebuked the servant for breaking the oath; the servant said, "Ordinary men must not be killed—how much less a magistrate?

sentences.zh: 此何等事，而使我為之。”

translations.literal: What sort of affair is this, that you would have me do it?"
translations.idiomatic: What kind of deed is this, that you would have me do it?"

sentences.zh: 若水乃仗劍徒步如武興，欲手刃曦，中道聞曦死，乃還。

translations.literal: Ruoshui then took sword in hand and went on foot to Wuxing, wishing to slay Xi with his own hand; halfway he heard Xi was dead and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui then took up his sword and walked to Wuxing to kill Xi himself; halfway he heard Xi was already dead and turned back.

sentences.zh: 人皆笑其狂，而壯其誌。

translations.literal: People all laughed at his madness, yet admired his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: People laughed at his madness, yet admired his resolve.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定十三年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiading 13.

sentences.zh: 時史彌遠柄國久，若水對策極論其奸，請罷之，更命賢相，否則必為宗社憂。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Miyuan had long held the state; in his examination answers Ruoshui exhaustively discussed his wickedness, asked that he be removed, and that a worthy chief minister be appointed—otherwise the altars of state would surely be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan had long dominated the state; in his palace examination Ruoshui denounced his treachery, demanded his removal and the appointment of a worthy chief minister, warning otherwise the altars of state would be imperiled.

sentences.zh: 考官置之末甲。

translations.literal: The examiners placed him last in the ranking.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners ranked him last.

sentences.zh: 策語播行，都士爭誦之。

translations.literal: His answer spread abroad, and the capital's scholars vied to recite it.
translations.idiomatic: His answers spread through the capital, and scholars vied to recite them.

sentences.zh: 彌遠怒，諭府尹使逆旅主人幾其出入，將置之罪，或為之解，乃已。

translations.literal: Miyuan was enraged and instructed the prefect to have innkeepers watch his comings and goings, intending to punish him; someone interceded and the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was enraged and told the prefect to have innkeepers watch his movements, intending to punish him; someone interceded and the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，應詔上封事曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, in response to an edict he submitted a sealed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, he submitted a sealed memorial in response to an edict:

sentences.zh: 行大義然後可以弭大謗，收大權然後可以固大位，除大奸然後可以息大難。

translations.literal: Only by acting on great righteousness can great slander be stilled; only by recovering great power can the great throne be secured; only by removing great traitors can great calamity be quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Great righteousness alone can still great slander; recovered power alone can secure the throne; removing great traitors alone can quell great calamity.

sentences.zh: 寧宗皇帝晏駕，濟王當繼大位者也，廢黜不聞於先帝，過失不聞於天下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong passed away, the Prince of Ji should have succeeded to the great throne; his deposition was not heard from the late emperor, nor were his faults heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong died, the Prince of Ji should have succeeded; his deposition was never announced by the late emperor, nor were any faults known to the realm.

sentences.zh: 史彌遠不利濟王之立，夜矯先帝之命，棄逐濟王，並殺皇孫，而奉迎陛下。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan did not want the Prince of Ji enthroned; by night he forged the late emperor's command, cast out the Prince of Ji, and killed the imperial grandson as well, then welcomed Your Majesty to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan opposed the Prince of Ji's enthronement; by night he forged the late emperor's command, deposed the prince, killed the imperial grandson, and installed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 曾未半年，濟王竟不幸於湖州。

translations.literal: In less than half a year the Prince of Ji met misfortune at Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year the Prince of Ji met his death at Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 揆以《春秋》之法，非弑乎？

translations.literal: Measured by the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals—is this not regicide?
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the Spring and Autumn Annals—is this not regicide?

sentences.zh: 非篡乎？

translations.literal: Is it not usurpation?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not usurpation?

sentences.zh: 非攘奪乎？

translations.literal: Is it not seizure by force?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not violent seizure?

sentences.zh: 當悖逆之初，天下皆歸罪彌遠而不敢歸過於陛下者，何也？

translations.literal: At the beginning of this treason, all under heaven blamed Miyuan and did not dare attribute fault to Your Majesty—why?
translations.idiomatic: When the treason began, the realm blamed Miyuan and dared not blame Your Majesty—why?

sentences.zh: 天下皆知倉卒之間，非陛下所得知，亦諒陛下必無是心也，亦料陛下必能清表妖氛，以雪先帝、濟王父子終天之憤。

translations.literal: All knew that in the sudden emergency Your Majesty could not have known, also trusted that Your Majesty surely had no such heart, and also expected that Your Majesty would surely be able to clear away evil influences and avenge the lifelong wrath of the late emperor and the Prince of Ji, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: All knew the sudden crisis lay beyond Your Majesty's knowledge, trusted you had no such intent, and expected you would purge the evil and avenge the late emperor and the Prince of Ji, father and son.

sentences.zh: 今逾年矣，而乾剛不決，威斷不行，無以大慰天下之望。

translations.literal: Now more than a year has passed, yet imperial firmness is undecided and authoritative judgment is not executed—there is no great consolation for the hopes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year has passed, yet you have not acted with firm resolve or authoritative judgment, and the realm's hopes remain unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 昔之信陛下之必無者，今或疑其有。

translations.literal: Those who once trusted that Your Majesty surely had no such heart now perhaps suspect that you do.
translations.idiomatic: Those who once trusted you innocent now suspect guilt.

sentences.zh: 昔之信陛下不知者，今或疑其知。

translations.literal: Those who once trusted that Your Majesty did not know now perhaps suspect that you did.
translations.idiomatic: Those who once believed you ignorant now suspect you knew.

sentences.zh: 陛下何以忍清明天日，而以此身受此汙辱也？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty bear clear heaven and bright sun and yet let your person receive this disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: How can you endure the clear sky and bright sun while your person wears this stain?

sentences.zh: 蓋亦求明是心於天下，而俾有辭於千古乎？

translations.literal: Is it not rather to make this heart clear to the realm and leave words for a thousand ages?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not rather to prove your heart to the realm and leave your name clean for posterity?

sentences.zh: 為陛下之計，莫若遵泰伯之至德，伯夷之清名，季子之高節，而後陛下之本心明於天下。

translations.literal: For Your Majesty's plan, nothing is better than following the utmost virtue of Taibo, the pure name of Boyi, and the lofty integrity of Jizi—then Your Majesty's true heart will be clear to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your best course is to follow Taibo's supreme virtue, Boyi's pure fame, and Jizi's lofty integrity—then your true heart will shine before the realm.

sentences.zh: 此臣所謂行大義以弭大謗，策之上也。

translations.literal: This is what your servant calls acting on great righteousness to still great slander—the highest policy.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I call acting on great righteousness to still great slander—the highest policy.

sentences.zh: 自古人君之失大權，鮮有不自廢立之際而盡失之。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when rulers have lost great power, few have not lost it entirely from the moment of deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, rulers who lost supreme power rarely failed to lose it entirely at the very moment of a forced succession.

sentences.zh: 當其廢立之間，威動天下。

translations.literal: At the moment of deposition and enthronement, their authority shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment their authority shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 既立則眇視人主，是故強臣挾恩以陵上，小人怙強以無上，久則內外相為一體，為上者喑默以聽其所為，日朘月削，殆有人臣之所不忍言者。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, they looked down on the ruler; therefore powerful ministers rely on favor to tower over their sovereign, petty men rely on strength to act as though there were no superior—after long time inner and outer become one body, and the one above keeps silent and listens to whatever they do, dwindling day by day and month by month, until there are things no subject should bear to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, they despise the ruler; powerful ministers lean on favor to tower over the throne, petty men on strength to act as though no superior existed—inside and outside merge, the ruler falls silent, power erodes daily, until even subjects cannot bear to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 威權一去，人主雖欲固其位，保其身，有不可得。

translations.literal: Once authority is gone, though the ruler may wish to secure his throne and preserve his person, he cannot obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Once authority is gone, the ruler cannot secure throne or person even if he wishes.

sentences.zh: 宣繒、薛極，彌遠之肺腑也；

translations.literal: Xuan Zhan and Xue Ji are Miyuan's heart and lungs;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Zhan and Xue Ji are Miyuan's inner circle;

sentences.zh: 王愈，其耳目也；

translations.literal: Wang Yu is his ears and eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu is his eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 盛章、李知孝，其鷹犬也；

translations.literal: Sheng Zhang and Li Zhixiao are his hawks and hounds;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Zhang and Li Zhixiao are his hawks and hounds;

sentences.zh: 馮榯，其爪牙也。

translations.literal: Feng Shan is his claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shan is his claws and teeth.

sentences.zh: 彌遠之欲行某事，害某人，則此數人者相與謀之，曷嚐有陛下之意行乎其間哉？

translations.literal: When Miyuan wishes to carry out some affair or harm some person, these several men plot together—when has Your Majesty's intent ever passed among them?
translations.idiomatic: When Miyuan wishes some deed done or some man harmed, these men plot together—when has Your Majesty's will ever entered their counsel?

sentences.zh: 臣以為不除此數凶，陛下非惟不足以弭謗，亦未可以必安其位，然則陛下何憚久而不為哉？

translations.literal: Your servant holds that unless these several villains are removed, Your Majesty will not only be unable to still slander but also cannot be sure of securing the throne—then why should Your Majesty hesitate long and not act?
translations.idiomatic: Unless these villains are removed, Your Majesty cannot still slander or secure the throne—why hesitate?

sentences.zh: 此臣所以謂收大權以定大位，策之次也。

translations.literal: This is why your servant says recover great power to fix the great throne—the second policy.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I call recovering great power to secure the throne—the second policy.

sentences.zh: 次而不行，又有一焉，曰：除大奸然後可以弭大難。

translations.literal: If the second is not carried out, there is yet another, namely: remove great traitors and then great calamity can be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: If the second fails, there is yet a third: remove great traitors to quell great calamity.

sentences.zh: 李全，一流民耳，寓食於我，兵非加多，土地非加廣，勢力非特盛也。

translations.literal: Li Quan is only a wandering refugee, living on our provisions; his troops are not greatly increased, his land not greatly expanded, his power not especially strong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan is only a refugee living on our grain; his troops, territory, and power have not greatly grown.

sentences.zh: 賈涉為帥，庸人耳，全不敢妄動，何也？

translations.literal: When Jia She was commander—a mediocre man—Quan did not dare act rashly; why?
