translations.idiomatic: Under Jia She, a mediocrity, Quan did not dare stir—why?

sentences.zh: 名正而言順也。

translations.literal: His title was correct and his words accorded with reason.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was legitimate and its word was righteous.

sentences.zh: 自陛下即位，乃敢倔強，何也？

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne he has dared to be stubborn—why?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession he has grown defiant—why?

sentences.zh: 彼有辭以用其眾也。

translations.literal: He has words with which to employ his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He has a rallying cry for his followers.

sentences.zh: 其意必曰：“濟王，先皇帝之子也，而彌遠放弑之。

translations.literal: His intent must be to say, "The Prince of Ji was the late emperor's son, yet Miyuan deposed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He surely says, "The Prince of Ji was the late emperor's son, yet Miyuan deposed and murdered him.

sentences.zh: 皇孫，先皇帝之孫也，而彌遠戕害之。”

translations.literal: The imperial grandson was the late emperor's grandson, yet Miyuan destroyed him."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson was the late emperor's grandson, yet Miyuan destroyed him."

sentences.zh: 其辭直，其勢壯，是以沿淮數十萬之師而不敢睥睨其鋒。

translations.literal: His words are straight and his momentum strong; therefore several hundred thousand troops along the Huai dare not look askance at his edge.
translations.idiomatic: His case is plain and his force strong; thus hundreds of thousands along the Huai dare not meet his challenge.

sentences.zh: 雖曰今暫無事，未也，安知其不一日羽檄飛馳，以濟王為辭，以討君側之惡為名？

translations.literal: Though one may say that for now there is temporarily no trouble, that is not yet so—who knows that one day urgent dispatches will not fly, taking the Prince of Ji as pretext and purging evil beside the ruler as name?
translations.idiomatic: One may say there is no trouble yet—but who knows urgent dispatches may not fly tomorrow, invoking the Prince of Ji and the cause of purging evil beside the throne?

sentences.zh: 彌遠之徒，死有餘罪，不可復惜，宗社生靈何辜焉？

translations.literal: Miyuan's faction deserve death many times over and cannot be regretted—but what crime have the altars of state and the living people committed?
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan's faction deserve death many times over—but what crime have the altars and the people committed?

sentences.zh: 陛下今日而誅彌遠之徒，則全無辭以用其眾矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty today executes Miyuan's faction, Quan will entirely lack words with which to employ his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Execute Miyuan's faction today, and Quan will lose every word with which to rally his followers.

sentences.zh: 上而不得，則思其次，次而不得，則思其下，悲夫！

translations.literal: If the highest cannot be obtained, then one thinks of the next; if the next cannot be obtained, then one thinks of the lower—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Unable to attain the highest aim, one settles for the next, then the next below—alas!

sentences.zh: 製置司不敢為附驛，卻還之。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission dared not dispatch it by courier and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission dared not forward it by courier and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 以格當改官，奏上，彌遠取筆橫抹之而罷。

translations.literal: By qualification he should have been promoted in office; when the memorial was submitted, Miyuan took the brush and crossed it out horizontally and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified for promotion, his memorial went up—but Miyuan crossed it out with a brush and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙間，召為太學博士，當對，草奏數千言，略曰：“寧宗不豫，彌遠急欲成其詐，此其心豈復願先帝之生哉？

translations.literal: Between the Jiading and Chunyou reigns he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; when he was to address the throne he drafted a memorial of several thousand words, in summary saying, "When Emperor Ningzong was ill, Miyuan urgently wished to complete his fraud—could his heart still have wished the late emperor to live?
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiading–Chunyou period he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; preparing to address the throne, he drafted a memorial of several thousand words, in essence: "When Emperor Ningzong fell ill, Miyuan rushed to complete his fraud—did he still wish the late emperor to live?

sentences.zh: 先帝不得正其終，陛下不得正其始，臣請發塚斫棺，取其屍斬之，以謝在天之靈。

translations.literal: The late emperor could not end properly, Your Majesty could not begin properly—I ask to open the tomb, split the coffin, take out the corpse and behead it, to appease the spirit in heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor could not die in peace, Your Majesty could not accede in peace—I ask to open his tomb, break the coffin, behead the corpse, and appease Heaven.

sentences.zh: 往年臣嚐上封事，請禪位近屬，以洗不義之汙，無路自達，今其書尚在，謹昧死以聞。”

translations.literal: In former years your servant once submitted a sealed memorial asking to abdicate in favor of a close kinsman to wash away unrighteous disgrace; there was no way to reach you, and the document still exists—your servant respectfully risks death to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Years ago I submitted a sealed memorial asking you to abdicate to a close kinsman and wash away unrighteous stain; it never reached you, and the document still exists—I risk death to present it again.

sentences.zh: 將對前一日，假筆吏於所親潘允恭，允恭素知若水好危言，諭筆吏使竊錄之。

translations.literal: On the day before he was to address the throne he borrowed a clerk from his intimate Pan Yonggong; Yonggong, knowing Ruoshui was fond of extreme words, instructed the clerk to copy it secretly.
translations.idiomatic: The day before his audience he borrowed a clerk from his friend Pan Yonggong; knowing Ruoshui's habit of extreme speech, Yonggong had the clerk copy the draft secretly.

sentences.zh: 允恭見之，懼並及禍，走告丞相喬行簡，亦大駭。

translations.literal: When Yonggong saw it he feared being caught in the calamity as well, ran to tell Chief Minister Qiao Xingjian, and Xingjian too was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, Yonggong feared being swept into disaster, fled to Chief Minister Qiao Xingjian, and Xingjian was also terrified.

sentences.zh: 翼日早朝，奏出若水通判寧國府。

translations.literal: The next day at the early audience a memorial was submitted ordering Ruoshui out as Vice Prefect of Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning at audience a memorial was submitted posting Ruoshui as Vice Prefect of Ningguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 退朝，召閣門舍人問曰：“今日有輪對官乎？”

translations.literal: After audience the emperor summoned the Gatekeeper Attendant and asked, "Is there an official scheduled to address the throne today?"
translations.idiomatic: After audience the emperor summoned the Gatekeeper Attendant: "Is there an official to address the throne today?"

sentences.zh: 舍人以若水對，行簡曰：“已得旨補外矣，可格班。”

translations.literal: The attendant answered with Ruoshui; Xingjian said, "An edict has already been obtained to post him outside; he may be dismissed from court."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant named Ruoshui; Xingjian said, "An edict already posts him outside; dismiss the audience."

sentences.zh: 若水袖其書待廡下，舍人諭使去，若水怏怏而退。

translations.literal: Ruoshui kept the document in his sleeve and waited beneath the corridor; the attendant instructed him to leave, and Ruoshui withdrew in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui waited in the corridor with the draft in his sleeve; the attendant told him to leave, and he withdrew, bitter.

sentences.zh: 自知不為時所容，到官數月，以言罷，遂不復仕，隱太湖之洞庭山。

translations.literal: Knowing he was not tolerated by the times, after several months in office he was dismissed for his words, and never again took office, hiding himself on Dongting Mountain at Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the times would not bear him, he was dismissed within months; he never served again and hid on Dongting Mountain at Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 賈似道在京湖，聞其名，辟參軍事。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao, in Jinghu, heard his name and recruited him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao in Jinghu heard his name and recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 若水雅思其鄉，乃起從其招，因西歸蜀。

translations.literal: Ruoshui had long yearned for his homeland; he then rose and accepted the summons, and returned west to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Long yearning for home, he accepted the summons and returned west to Shu.

sentences.zh: 居山中，有盜夜劫之，若水危坐不動，盜擊其首，流血被麵，亦不動，乃舍去。

translations.literal: Living in the mountains, there were bandits who robbed him by night; Ruoshui sat upright without moving; the bandits struck his head and blood covered his face, yet he still did not move, and they then left him.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains bandits robbed him by night; Ruoshui sat upright without moving; they struck his head until blood covered his face, yet he did not stir, and they left.

sentences.zh: 若水為學務躬行，恥為空言。

translations.literal: Ruoshui in learning devoted himself to practice and was ashamed of empty words.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship Ruoshui devoted himself to practice and despised empty talk.

sentences.zh: 削木為主，大書曰“自古以來忠臣孝子義夫節婦之位”，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: He carved wooden tablets and wrote large upon them, "The place of loyal ministers, filial sons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives since antiquity," and sacrificed to them at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He carved wooden tablets inscribed "The place of loyal ministers, filial sons, righteous husbands, and chaste women since antiquity," and sacrificed to them each season.

sentences.zh: 有一子，膂力絕人，築山砦，以兵捍衛鄉井。

translations.literal: He had one son of extraordinary strength who built a mountain stockade and used troops to defend the local community.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son of extraordinary strength who built a mountain stockade and raised troops to defend the countryside.

sentences.zh: 砦破，舉家遇害。

translations.literal: When the stockade fell, the whole family was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the stockade fell, the whole family perished.

sentences.zh: 僧真寶，代州人，為五台山僧正。

translations.literal: The monk Zhenbao, a man of Dai Prefecture, was abbot of Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhenbao, a native of Dai Prefecture, was abbot of Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 學佛，能外死生。

translations.literal: He studied Buddhism and could set life and death aside.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Buddhism and had mastered detachment from life and death.

sentences.zh: 靖康之擾，與其徒習武事於山中。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Jingkang, he and his disciples practiced military affairs in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang turmoil he and his disciples trained in military affairs in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 欽宗召對便殿，眷齎隆縟。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong summoned him to audience in the side hall and bestowed rich gifts with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong summoned him to the side hall and lavished rich gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 真寶還山，益聚兵助討。

translations.literal: Zhenbao returned to the mountain and gathered more troops to aid the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenbao returned to the mountain and gathered more troops to aid the resistance.

sentences.zh: 州不守，敵眾大至，晝夜拒之，力不敵，寺舍盡焚。

translations.literal: When the prefecture could not be held, the enemy host came in great force; day and night he resisted them, but strength did not match them and the monastery buildings were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture fell, the enemy came in force; he resisted day and night until outmatched, and the monastery burned to the ground.

sentences.zh: 酋下令生致真寶，至則抗詞無撓，酋異之，不忍殺也。

translations.literal: The enemy leader ordered that Zhenbao be taken alive; when he arrived he spoke defiant words without yielding; the leader marveled at him and could not bear to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy leader ordered Zhenbao taken alive; brought before him, Zhenbao spoke without yielding; the leader marveled and could not bear to kill him.

sentences.zh: 使郡守劉騊誘勸百方，終不顧，且曰：“吾法中有口四之罪，吾既許宋皇帝以死，豈當妄言也？”

translations.literal: He had the prefect Liu Tao try every means to persuade him, yet in the end Zhenbao would not heed him, and added, "In my Law there is the offense of the four mouths; I have already promised the Song emperor I would die—how could I speak falsely?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Liu Tao tried every persuasion, yet Zhenbao would not listen, saying, "My Law forbids false speech; I have promised the Song emperor my death—how can I speak falsely?"

sentences.zh: 怡然受戮。

translations.literal: He accepted execution with composure.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted execution calmly.

sentences.zh: 北人聞見者歎異焉。

translations.literal: Northerners who saw and heard it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners who witnessed it marveled.

sentences.zh: 時萬安僧亦起兵，舉旗曰“降魔”，又曰：“時危聊作將，事定復為僧。”

translations.literal: At that time the monk of Wan'an also raised troops, raising a banner saying "Subdue Demons," and also saying, "In peril one briefly becomes a general; when the matter is settled one returns to being a monk."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk of Wan'an also raised troops under a banner reading "Subdue Demons," saying, "In crisis one briefly becomes a general; when peace returns, one becomes a monk again."

sentences.zh: 旋亦敗死。

translations.literal: He too was soon defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: He too was soon defeated and died.

sentences.zh: 徐道明，常州天慶觀道士也。

translations.literal: Xu Daoming was a Daoist of the Tianqing Abbey in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoming was a Daoist priest of the Tianqing Abbey in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為管轄，賜紫。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent and was granted the purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He served as superintendent and was granted the purple robe.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，北兵圍城，道明謁郡守姚訔請曰：“事急矣，君侯計將安出？”

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou, when the northern armies besieged the city, Daoming called on the prefect Yao Yin and asked, "The matter is urgent—what plan does my lord intend?"
translations.idiomatic: In Deyou 1, as northern armies besieged the city, Daoming visited Prefect Yao Yin: "Matters are urgent—what is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 訔曰：“內無食，外無援，死守而已。”

translations.literal: Yin said, "Within there is no food, without there is no aid—we can only die defending the city."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "No food within, no aid without—we can only die defending the walls."

sentences.zh: 道明亟還，慨然告其徒曰：“姚公誓與城俱亡，吾屬亦不失為義士。”

translations.literal: Daoming hurried back and told his disciples in emotion, "Lord Yao has sworn to perish with the city; we too shall not fail to be men of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Daoming returned and told his disciples, "Prefect Yao swears to die with the city; we too shall not fail to be men of righteousness."

sentences.zh: 乃取觀之文籍置石函，藏坎中。

translations.literal: He then took the abbey's documents, placed them in a stone casket, and hid them in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the abbey's records in a stone casket and buried them in a pit.

sentences.zh: 兵屠城，道明危坐焫香，讀《老子》書。

translations.literal: When the soldiers slaughtered the city, Daoming sat upright burning incense and reading the Book of Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: When the army sacked the city, Daoming sat upright burning incense and reading the Book of Laozi.

sentences.zh: 兵使之拜，不顧，誦聲琅然；

translations.literal: The soldiers ordered him to bow; he paid no heed, and his recitation rang clear;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers ordered him to bow; he ignored them, his recitation ringing clear;

sentences.zh: 以刃脅之，不為動，遂死焉。

translations.literal: they threatened him with blades yet he did not move, and so he died.
translations.idiomatic: they threatened him with blades, yet he did not stir, and so he died.
